title: Harness delegation ledger record
description: One record per delegation. Append-only, one JSON object per line (.jsonl). This is the training signal for outcome-weighted agent selection (14-orchestration.md §8) AND the corpus for replay-eval (Q1). Outcome history cannot be reconstructed retroactively, so record from the first delegation.
_minimum_write: A perfect schema that nothing writes to loses to an ugly one that does. REQUIRED is therefore the minimum viable write: trace id, stage/task, producing agent, outcome. Everything else is recommended and can be backfilled — except run_id/event_id/parent_id, which cannot be reconstructed later and are the reason the trace fields are in the required set at all. Ledger writes on every rejection are a HARD PRECONDITION for running beyond the two-stage pilot: without them this is a pipeline that runs once, not a harness.

ts.description: When the delegation resolved, not when it started.

run_id.description: One id per harness run, stamped at FIND. Groups every event in the run.

event_id.description: One id per recorded step. Attribution attaches to an event, not to a stage — the stage is derived from whoever owned this event.

parent_id.description: The event this one derives from. Walking parent_id backward from a failing verdict to the earliest event whose output later events consumed unchanged gives the FIRST DIVERGENCE mechanically. This is what converts blame attribution from a judgement into a lookup. MUST be stamped at FIND — it cannot be reconstructed from rejection text afterwards.

evidence_available.description: Was the evidence needed to avoid this defect present in the stage's inputs? If FALSE this is a harness or contract finding caused by evidence starvation, and it MUST be excluded from agent weighting regardless of attribution — weighting away from a starved agent is the wrong correction, because the replacement inherits the same starvation. Answerable from the trace rather than by judgement, which is why it supersedes attribution_confidence as the primary exclusion rule.

task_class.description: The routing key, and the aggregation unit. Format <stage>.<work-or-finding-type>, e.g. 'A.mutually-exclusive-claim', 'C.scope-slicing', 'F.slice-implement', 'G.spec-gap'. A free-text value here makes the whole ledger unaggregatable, which is why the pattern is enforced. `council.<slug>` is allowed for harness-council lenses and memos (doc 34).

surface.description: Dotted surface the work was routed on, matching an agent's `surfaces:` entry. Dotted so prefixes are matchable: 'ads.audience-sync' is covered by an agent declaring 'ads'.

agent.description: Resolved agent name, or 'skill:<name>' when resolution step 1 applied, or 'none' when no delegation was needed. Council lenses use 'council.<lens>'.

resolution_step.description: Which step of the resolution order picked this. Step 5 (new agent proposed) should be rare; a rising share of step 5 is the sprawl warning signal.

outcome.description: resolved-clean is the only positive weight. 'escalated' means the cycle budget was exhausted.

cycle.description: Iteration number within the current gate. >2 should not occur; the budget is two before escalation.

rejected_by.description: The gate (G1-G5) or stage that rejected. Distinct from where the rejection was routed.

routed_to.description: The stage judged to have PRODUCED the defect, per the §5 routing table. Not the stage that found it.

attribution.description: What this rejection is attributable to. 'agent-event' — the agent owning the first-divergence event produced the defect. 'missing-gate' — a check that would have caught the defect in transit did not exist; this is a HARNESS defect, routed to the harness, and it must not dilute any agent's weight. 'unknown' — first divergence could not be located, usually meaning the trace is incomplete. Replaces the earlier 'shared' value, which was a modelling artifact of missing instrumentation: what looked like shared blame decomposes into two sole attributions at different layers, and conflating them discarded records that were recoverable.

exploration.description: True when the orchestrator deliberately took a non-top candidate. Keeps a worse outcome attributable rather than mysterious, and prevents exploration from being read as a regression.

human.description: Who adjudicated, when a human gate was involved. Enables tracking per-reviewer approval rate, which is the habituation health metric.

human_rationale.description: WHY the human decided as they did, not just what they decided. The gates are the reliability backstop and the least-designed surface in the framework: a human arriving at '14 green checks, agents raised nothing' is primed exactly the way the 93pp detection-collapse study describes. Recording rationale makes gate quality reviewable instead of assumed.

gate_override.description: Did the human decide against what the agents recommended? Tracked as a CALIBRATION signal: a near-zero override rate is not evidence of trust, it may be rubber-stamping. This is the human-side twin of 'high inter-reviewer agreement is a warning, not a pass'.

source_as_of.description: For a finding: the `as_of` of every source it depends on, keyed by artifact id. FIND establishes truth at T; BUILD lands weeks later. This project's own legal register went stale in FOUR DAYS — verified on the 21st, overtaken by a platform answer on the 25th, still reading 'not yet requested'. A gate re-validates whether these sources moved before proceeding, so DECIDE cannot commit against a FIND that is no longer true.

model.description: Model actually served, not requested. For Pantheon runs read this from the run.started event, NOT runs.model, which records the request.

tokens.description: Output tokens for this delegation. Feeds per-stage cost attribution and the auto-pause caps.

minutes.description: Wall-clock minutes for this delegation, from tool timestamps. With tokens it makes slow build, test, mutation and review loops visible (46-build-and-review-loop-budget.md §6).

prompt_chars.description: Characters in the prompt sent to a reviewer (wc -c of the brief). Target 15,000 or fewer: the diff, the question and file pointers, no pasted file bodies (doc 46 §5).

eval_candidate.description: True when an earlier stage should have caught this and did not — e.g. a spec gap surfaced at Verify that Audit missed. These are the highest-value replay-eval cases and the reason the ledger doubles as the eval corpus.

notes.description: One or two sentences of why. Not a transcript.

evidence.description: Snapshot paths, URLs, or commits this event rests on. The snapshot path is the one that links doc 33 records to the ledger.
